notesStmt.note: A note on the verso, in an unknown hand (possibly that of Horace Traubel), reads "Feb 18, 1888." It is possible that this manuscript was written on that date, but it was almost certainly created around that time, just prior to the poem's publication.
This is a fair copy draft of the poem "Paumanok," which was first published in the New York Herald on February 29, 1888. The poem was then reprinted in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: Paumanok.
lg.l:
One side thy inland ocean laving, broad, with
copious commerce, steamers, sails,

And one the Atlantic's wind caressing, fierce or
gentle—mighty hulls dark⹀gliding in
the distance:

Isle of sweet brooks of drinking⹀water—healthy
air and soil!
Isle of the salty shore and breeze and brine!
